tools.name: evalspill
tools.description: Drop the file you fine-tuned on and the eval set you scored; find the eval rows whose text already appears INSIDE a training row, see the shared passage highlighted in both, and leave with a byte-exact cleaned eval file. QUEUE ORDER WAS FOLLOWED: this is the `leakspot` entry, top of the queue, unblocked for the first time — standing-note rule 2 held it while chunkforge (2026-08-10) shared its static-embedding engine, and on 2026-08-18 that is eight days. The sensor debt was considered and deliberately not paid: IDEAS.md records that the 2026-08-11 hunt spent three adversarial rounds killing all eight candidates and asks for a hand-added idea rather than another speculative hunt. THIRTEEN AGENTS RAN (six research lenses each attacked by an independent refuter, plus a synthesist; 1.36M subagent tokens) AND THE PITCH'S ENGINE, ITS HEADLINE AND ITS MARKET CLAIM WERE EACH INDEPENDENTLY FALSIFIED. (1) MINHASH IS THE WRONG PRIMITIVE AND WAS DELETED. Contamination is asymmetric containment, not symmetric similarity: a 100-word eval row sitting verbatim inside a 1,000-word training document scores Jaccard 0.089 against containment 1.00, and at that Jaccard the LSH candidate probability at b=8,r=4 is 0.0003 — the pair never becomes a candidate, so no downstream stage can rescue it. Reproduced digit-for-digit by three agents. Every published recipe (GPT-3 TOKEN-MATCH, PaLM NGRAM-MATCH, Llama 2 TOKEN-EXTEND, ConTAM LONGEST-MATCH, Llama 3 5.1.4) normalises by the EVALUATION sample. (2) THE SPEC'S '13-gram CHARACTER shingles' WAS THE SINGLE MOST DANGEROUS DEFECT, caught by three independent refuters: measured, 13-CHARACTER shingles are shared by 1.93%-58% of completely unrelated document pairs depending on corpus, 8-WORD grams by 0.0020%, 13-WORD grams by 0.0000%. It also destroys the tool's main defence against a false positive — showing the reader the shared passage — because at thirteen characters that passage is a stopword phrase. (3) N IS ADAPTIVE, WHICH IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN A REFINEMENT. GPT-3's own rule is the 5th-percentile eval row length in words, floor 8, ceiling 13; a FIXED N=13 reports '0% contaminated' on TruthfulQA, 84% of whose rows are shorter than that — a confident false negative on exactly the claim the tool exists to protect. (4) THE FLAGSHIP HEADLINE IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE. 'You score 91%, but 12% leaked, so on the clean subset it is 84%' cannot happen: the clean-subset mean is pinned to [(o-c)/(1-c), min(1,o/(1-c))], so at o=0.91,c=0.12 the largest possible fall is 1.23 points and 91->84 needs c=43.75%. The tool prints the BOUND, in BOTH directions — GPT-3 Appendix C anticipates the upward one verbatim — gated on the metric being an unweighted mean of per-row scores in [0,1], with a Wilson-interval gate that suppresses the comparison when the two subsets are within noise. (5) 'NOBODY SELLS THIS' WAS FALSE AND A FREE CLIENT-SIDE INCUMBENT EXISTS. jsonlkit.com ships /jsonl-leakage-detector and /jsonl-near-duplicates, free and fully in-browser. I READ ITS SHIPPED tool.js (318,594 chars, fetched 2026-08-18) RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE REPORT: its leakage detector is whole-key EXACT string equality via index[k] after optional lowercase / whitespace-collapse / punctuation-strip, with four modes (whole record, one field, first user prompt, whole conversation). No n-grams, no containment, no fuzzy matching of any kind — so an eval question inside a longer training document is invisible to it, as is one changed word — and it emits leakage-report.txt only, never a cleaned file, while telling the user to 'remove these before you report a score'. Its near-duplicate tool is real MinHash (H=64, 16 bands x 4 rows, word shingles k=5) but SINGLE-PANE, i.e. intra-file dedup. So browser MinHash is NOT unattempted and the copy never claims it is; the narrow true claim is that no free client-side tool does cross-file n-gram containment with a cleaned-file output. (6) THE NAME CHANGED. 'leakspot' collides with a published academic JS memory-leak detector (doi 10.1002/spe.2406) and sits in the breach-lookup namespace where the ML meaning cannot rank; 'evalspill' cleared four checks (npm 404, evalspill.com unregistered per Verisign RDAP, zero GitHub repos, empty SERP). Two proposed alternatives were killed on inspection — overlapcheck.com is a live ETF overlap calculator and spancheck is a golangci-lint linter with 83 stars. BUGS THE BUILD CAUGHT ON ITSELF: the FIRST sample generator produced 487 matches out of 500, every one a CORRECT detection of a genuinely shared phrase and all of them noise, because a slot grammar of twenty subject phrases cannot help repeating eight-word runs; the SECOND, with rejection sampling, could not finish at all, because a single constraint phrase is itself eight words drawn from twelve options so after twelve rows every such run is used. The fix is structural rather than statistical — a per-row reference woven through each sentence so no eight-word run can avoid one, asserted in the generator rather than assumed — after which the sample yields EXACTLY the fifty planted rows and nothing else. Two further collisions were then found and fixed by measurement: runs straddling the question/answer join (the answer now carries a leading reference) and runs straddling the boilerplate-footer junction (the footer is attached behind a fresh reference so its OWN runs stay identical across rows, which is what gives them a document frequency the filter can see). The source-hygiene gate caught a literal NUL byte in a test file written during this run. The structural no-verdict gate fired on the sentence 'It does not tell you a model cheated' — the denial the whole tool is built around — and was narrowed to identifier-shaped matches. VERIFIED IN THE BROWSER, NOT ASSERTED: the shipped sample yields EXACTLY 50 of 488 scorable rows through the real worker, matching the pinned unit test; N is chosen as 13 with 12 rows reported too short to score rather than counted as clean; the bound renders as 90.0% -> 88.9%...100.0%, at most 1.1 points down, and the measured clean subset lands EXACTLY on the bound's floor because the flagged rows all scored 1; 9 word runs are dropped as boilerplate, which is exactly the number of 13-grams in the 21-word planted footer; eval.clean.jsonl is 450 rows with ZERO byte-exact mismatches against the original file, dropping precisely the 50 plants; the exported report is 40 KB with 0 scripts, 0 links, 0 src attributes and 0 on* handlers; the CSV carries a UTF-8 BOM checked ON THE BYTES because Blob.text() strips it by spec; all three modals pass all five dismissal exits at 375px including a real touch-type PointerEvent sequence and a keyboard path (15/15) at 44x44, plus the drawer's own exits; the feedback widget's button survives four full re-renders, proving the footer memoisation is load-bearing; and a full run issues requests for the page's own assets and its own samples and NOTHING else. A MOBILE DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN THE BROWSER: at 375px the four numeric columns ate the width and pushed the shared passage — the one thing the reader must be able to read — into a horizontal scroll they had to discover; the table now stacks into cards below 40rem. HONEST GAPS: stage 2, the semantic detector for REWORDED rows, is NOT in this build — its asset was extracted and verified against the real ONNX runtime to 3.6e-8 and calibrated (AUC 0.953, precision@5 62.5%, and a finding the research missed: mean-pooling converges to the corpus centroid so background cosine reaches 0.789 at 4,000 characters and CHUNKING IS MANDATORY), but it needs a 5.8 MB vendored table and a second engine, and shipping both half-finished serves nobody; it is recorded in EXPANSION_IDEAS.md with every measurement intact. The interface states plainly that reworded rows are not found. Removing rows from the TRAINING side is also not offered and the interface says why. The analytics beacon could not be observed delivering a request from the sandboxed preview, so it is verified structurally; the feedback widget WAS observed mounting. Desktop screenshots came back blank whenever the page was scrolled — a Browser-pane capture artefact — so desktop layout below the fold was verified by DOM geometry rather than by eye. 170 tests, one runtime dependency.
browser_apis: File.stream() + getReader() — the training file is never held as one string, and `for await ... of` a ReadableStream is deliberately avoided because async stream iteration is Safari 27, i.e. essentially no iPhone in the field

fflate Gunzip rather than DecompressionStream('gzip'): `cat shard-00.jsonl.gz shard-01.jsonl.gz > train.gz` is routine in sharded ML pipelines and produces a legal MULTI-MEMBER stream, so a decoder stopping at the first member would scan half the file and then report a confident 'no overlap found' — and the gzip ISIZE trailer cannot catch it, because with equal shards a truncated read passes

A byte-level record splitter rather than a text-level one: the offsets it produces are the offsets File.slice() needs, and UTF-8 is self-synchronising so no ASCII byte — not the newline, not the comma, not the quote — can occur inside a multi-byte sequence. Verified by replaying every document at every possible chunk boundary

Quote-aware splitting for CSV, because a newline inside a quoted field is ordinary data in a CSV of eval questions and a splitter that ignores it turns one record into nine — and this tool's whole output is a count of rows

A charCodeAt word scanner, never toLowerCase().replace().split(): measured, the naive path costs more in `split` alone than every hash in the pipeline combined, over a file that may be gigabytes. Non-ASCII words fall back to toLowerCase, because `| 0x20` is only a lowercase operation for ASCII

Smart quotes, em dashes and CJK punctuation treated as separators, or a document quoted with U+2019 and the same document quoted with an apostrophe share no word at the boundary and a real verbatim copy goes unreported

A rolling Rabin-Karp fingerprint over pre-hashed words with a murmur fmix32 avalanche — NOT hash-wasm, which measured 104-211x slower per shingle because the JS/WASM boundary dominates at 50-byte payloads. verisum's hash-wasm precedent is whole-file hashing, the opposite workload

The n-gram window RESET AT EVERY RECORD BOUNDARY, or the scan emits phantom runs spanning the end of one row and the start of the next — and, when the text comes from a serialised record, runs made partly of JSON key names that every record shares

One open-addressed Uint32Array over eval n-gram fingerprints at load factor 0.5, with parallel arrays for row and position and a chained entry list: measured 8.3-8.7 bytes per element against 24-41 for a JS Set, which on a million n-grams is the difference between a working tab and a dead one

A ~2 MB Bloom prefilter whose justification is CACHE RESIDENCY rather than memory — the miss path is overwhelmingly the common one on a training file — and which is documented as lossless so it cannot later be 'optimised away' on the belief that it changes results

Two streaming passes when the boilerplate filter is on: the first counts how many DISTINCT training records contain each eval run, the second applies only those under GPT-3's cap of max(10, 0.1% of corpus). It cannot be one pass without either keeping every hit — a single boilerplate phrase produces millions — or being unable to withdraw a phrase that turns out to be boilerplate near the end of the file
ZERO training bytes retained: a match stores a coverage bit and, for a bounded number of rows, one 240-character excerpt. Nothing else of the training file survives the pass

Containment and LONGEST MATCH both normalised by the EVAL row rather than the pair, which is the entire reason this is not MinHash — and longest match is the primary displayed number because it is the only one a human can check by reading it

A field picker that descends into nested objects, because lm-evaluation-harness --log_samples nests the dataset row at doc.* and splats metrics over the top level with no `score` key — so a flat picker finds nothing to compare in the commonest eval-output format there is

Near-constant fields excluded by default: a production SFT JSONL carries an identical `system` string on every row, and comparing serialised records reports ~97% contamination between two perfectly clean files. This is the single most likely way a tool like this ships broken
A score column accepted only when every value is a per-row number in [0,1], so a 0-100 percentage, a macro-average or a BLEU is REFUSED rather than silently mis-bounded

eval.clean.jsonl built by concatenating the ORIGINAL BYTES of surviving records — spans widened to the next record's start so line terminators survive — never by re-serialising, which would reorder keys, change escaping and rewrite line endings while looking correct

First-party RFC 4180 CSV writer: control characters become visible escapes so one record is always one physical line, and the formula-injection guard EXEMPTS complete numeric literals, because almost every column this tool writes is numeric and the naive guard turns them all into text

A self-contained report.html built entirely with createElement and textContent — every value in it comes from files evalspill did not write and the report is opened from file://, so string templating would let a training corpus put script into the report about itself

A permanent aria-live region OUTSIDE #app, and focus preserved across a full re-render via stable data-focus-key attributes, because render() calls app.replaceChildren() and ticking a field chip would otherwise drop focus to <body> with the element just operated on detached

Both the footer and the event-log drawer MEMOISED, because both are built inside render(): the hosted feedback widget's link dies on the first re-render without the first, and the drawer silently stops opening without the second

Build-output gates in CI with the build BEFORE the tests so they cannot silently skip: no indexedDB/getDirectory-as-a-call/sessionStorage/document.cookie in dist/**, exactly one localStorage key checked as a STRING LITERAL because minification hoists the identifier, no console.* survivors, an absolute-URL allowlist by ORIGIN containing only pages the tool LINKS to (a link is not a request), all origins in both CSP directives, manifest-src named explicitly, and an apple-touch-icon whose pixels are decoded and alpha-checked

A negation-aware honesty gate over every user-facing string including the meta descriptions and JSON-LD, asserted POSITIVELY as well as negatively — a gate that only forbids claims passes on a page that simply omits the caveat — plus a contrast gate that COMPUTES WCAG ratios for every text token against every background it can sit on, and for the amber highlight the shared passage sits on

Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell with both samples precached and NO runtimeCaching, because workbox-expiration pulls IndexedDB into the bundle and would falsify the 'nothing is written to disk' promise)

tools.name: epochcost
tools.description: Count a fine-tuning JSONL with the model's real tokenizer, find the records longer than the TRAINING EXAMPLE limit (which is not the context window), and price an epoch. QUEUE ORDER WAS FOLLOWED FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE 08-09: epochcost was the top entry and had been blocked by standing-note rule 2 on 08-15 and 08-16 because chunkforge (2026-08-10) shares the tokenizer engine and runledger (2026-08-09) shares the streaming-NDJSON-to-a-cost-figure architecture; on 2026-08-17 those are 7 and 8 days old, the week has passed, and the entry was unblocked. The sensor debt was considered and deliberately not paid: IDEAS.md records that the 2026-08-11 hunt spent three adversarial rounds and killed all eight candidates, and asks for a hand-added idea rather than another speculative hunt. TWELVE AGENTS RAN (six investigators, each attacked by an independent refuter, 2.09M subagent tokens) and SIX FINDINGS CHANGED THE PRODUCT RATHER THAN THE CODE. (1) OPENAI IS WINDING DOWN FINE-TUNING, so the spec's OpenAI-first framing would have shipped dead. Its own pricing page carries the banner 'OpenAI is winding down the fine-tuning platform. The platform is no longer accessible to new users'; the deprecations page dates it 7 May 2026 no new orgs, 2 Jul 2026 no org without fine-tuned inference in 60 days, 6 Jan 2027 nobody — about twenty weeks after this ships. The FILE-shaped problem is untouched, so the tool is provider-neutral: Together, Fireworks and Azure lead and OpenAI is one clearly-labelled legacy row. (2) A DIRECT INCUMBENT EXISTS AND THE SPEC'S LINE ABOUT IT WAS FALSE. jsonlkit.com/token-counter is free, client-side, takes a dropped .jsonl and estimates fine-tune cost, so 'the free counters cannot take a file' is refuted and appears nowhere in the shipped copy. It is beatable on four MEASURED points, which are now the entire product thesis: it uses a ~4.0 chars/token heuristic by its own admission, it counts the raw JSON line including the 'role'/'content' keys the model never sees, it omits the per-message chat framing, and — decisively — it checks the INFERENCE context window (128k) where the fine-tuning example limit is 65,536, so it green-lights records the trainer will still cut. A refuter then read its shipped tool.js and found it does NOT stream: the whole file goes through readFileAsText into a textarea's .value behind a confirm() over 10 MB. (3) THE TRUNCATION PREMISE IS CONFIRMED AND STRONGER THAN THE SPEC KNEW. OpenAI's own words: 'Examples longer than the default are truncated to the maximum context length, which removes tokens from the end of the training example.' The end of a chat record is the assistant turn, and the training limit is exactly HALF the inference window. (4) THE BILLING FORMULA IS CAPPED PER RECORD AND THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION IS WRONG. Billable tokens are sum(min(record, limit)) x epochs, not sum(record) x epochs — a 200,000-token record is billed at 65,536. Summing raw lengths overestimates on exactly the files that have over-limit records, which is this tool's flagship case. Proven on the shipped sample in the browser: 1,884,876 billable against 2,196,051 raw, and both numbers are shown. (5) gpt-tokenizer 3.4.0's dist/cl100k_base.js IS A MISLABELLED o200k_base BUILD, reproduced independently here: loaded in isolation it reports vocabularySize 200006 and encodes 'hello world' as [24912,2375] where cl100k gives [15339,1917]; the file is 2,048,099 bytes against real cl100k ranks of ~1.16 MB and sha256 8173d245... matches what unpkg serves, so the bug is live. Every GPT-4, GPT-3.5 and embedding count built on it is silently wrong with plausible ids and no error. This build pins 4.0.0's ESM subpaths and REFUSES TO START on an encoding whose ids do not match a pinned pair. (6) THE PADDING-WASTE HEADLINE IS REFUTED AND CUT: providers bill tokens in the FILE x epochs and padding is not in the file. FURTHER CORRECTIONS INHERITED FROM THE REFUTERS: DecompressionStream('gzip') is unsound on multi-member gzip and 'cat shard-00.jsonl.gz shard-01.jsonl.gz > all.gz' is routine in sharded ML pipelines, so fflate's Gunzip ships instead — and Node's DecompressionStream is non-conformant, so a vitest test of that path would have returned a FALSE PASS; davinci-002/babbage-002 fine-tuning was shut down 2024-10-28 and o4-mini is billed per HOUR, so none of the three may appear in a token-cost table; the Azure Retail Prices API has no CORS headers and is unusable from a static page. MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: end-to-end throughput (line split + JSON.parse + BPE) is 14.8 MB/s single-threaded with BPE at 97% of it, so 1.2 GB is ~1.3 min on one thread and under a minute on a pool — the spec's '5-10 minutes' was pessimistic. An agent's claim that base64 content collapses gpt-tokenizer to 0.43 MiB/s DID NOT REPRODUCE (measured 16.8 MB/s on random base64, faster than prose), so no adaptive-cache complexity was added; a live measured ETA handles any slow content generically. Chunk sizes measured: o200k 2,012,571 B raw / 1,028,715 gz, cl100k 951,254 / 442,560, p50k 474,572 / 203,221, and o200k_harmony reuses the o200k chunk for 1,125 B — the spec's 'cl100k 2.05 MB' was the mislabelled build. Hugging Face CORS echoes the Origin on both hops; meta-llama/* and google/gemma-* return 401 anonymously so Llama ships via the named ungated unsloth mirror. BUGS THE BUILD CAUGHT ON ITSELF: encode() THROWS on any content containing '<|im_start|>', which real training data contains, and one such record would end a scan of two million — and the obvious fix (allowedSpecial:'all') encodes a content string that IS the marker as the single id 200003, an undercount, so the shipped option is an empty disallowed-set which both stops the throw and counts it as the six ordinary tokens it is. costCents rounded to whole cents, printing '$0.00' for a real sub-cent charge — which reads as free rather than cheap, a different claim. THE EVENT-LOG DRAWER STOPPED OPENING AFTER THE FIRST RENDER, found in the browser and not in the unit tests: mountEventLog is called from header(), which render() rebuilds on every interaction, so it appended a NEW drawer to document.body each time — three were live, the toggle controlled the newest and getElementById returned the first. Same class of bug as the memoised footer, same fix, now gated. Two build gates were themselves wrong: the tokenizer-import gate missed DYNAMIC imports, and the banned-API scan fired on the RANK TABLES, which contain 'sessionStorage' and 'XMLHttpRequest' as genuine vocabulary tokens — the gate was scanning data as if it were code, and the exemption is now narrow and itself asserted. VERIFIED IN THE BROWSER, NOT ASSERTED: the shipped sample yields EXACTLY 8 over-limit records of 612 through the real gzip reader, worker pool and tokenizer, matching the pinned unit test; over-limit.jsonl is exactly 8 parseable JSON records; over-limit.csv shows record 442 losing 16,845 tokens of which ALL 16,845 are assistant tokens, which is the product thesis on real data; the exported report is 5.2 KB with no script, link or src; all three modals pass all four dismissal exits at 375px with real touch-type PointerEvents (12/12) at 44x44, plus the drawer's own exits; and a full run issues requests for the page's own assets and its own sample and NOTHING else. HONEST GAPS: the open-model (Hugging Face) tokenizer path was NOT exercised end-to-end in the browser — it is wired and typed but no run was made against a live tokenizer.json, and a refuter measured that path at 0.24 MiB/s on SentencePiece models, ~79x slower than gpt-tokenizer, which is why the interface measures throughput and shows an ETA before committing; the multi-member gzip claim is implemented on fflate's documented behaviour and was not differentially tested against a concatenated archive in a browser; and the analytics beacon and feedback widget were verified structurally (the footer link mounts and survives re-render) rather than by observing a delivered request. 115 tests, three runtime dependencies.
browser_apis: File.stream() + getReader() — a multi-gigabyte training file is never held as one string, and `for await ... of` a ReadableStream is deliberately avoided because async stream iteration is Safari 27, i.e. essentially no iPhone in the field

fflate Gunzip rather than DecompressionStream('gzip'): `cat shard-00.jsonl.gz shard-01.jsonl.gz > train.gz` is routine in sharded ML pipelines and produces a legal MULTI-MEMBER stream, so a decoder that stops at the first member would print a confident dollar figure for half the file — and the gzip ISIZE trailer cannot catch it, because with equal shards a truncated read passes

One reader worker cutting only at line boundaries, feeding N counter workers over MessagePorts with a TWO-CREDIT-PER-LANE protocol and transferable ArrayBuffers. The backpressure is the point: reading runs at ~1,800 MB/s and counting at ~15 MB/s, so without credits the queued chunks are the whole file in memory — the exact failure streaming exists to prevent

gpt-tokenizer 4.0.0 ESM subpaths, dynamic-imported one encoding at a time and ONLY inside the worker — Vite builds a worker in a separate Rollup pass, so an encoding imported on both sides is emitted twice; a dist gate asserts each rank table appears exactly once and that the entry chunk stays under 200 kB
A boot-time tokenizer self-check that REFUSES TO COUNT on a mismatch, because gpt-tokenizer 3.4.0 shipped a cl100k build that was actually o200k and nothing about that failure is visible at runtime

encode() with an EMPTY disallowed-special set: the default throws on any content containing '<|im_start|>', and allowedSpecial:'all' silently collapses a content string that IS the marker to one token instead of six

@huggingface/tokenizers over a tokenizer.json fetched from the Hub, with .ids.length (encode() returns an Encoding object, and .length on it is undefined, so a count would be NaN rather than throw) and add_special_tokens:false, or the post-processor prepends a BOS to every content string and inflates the file by one token per message

The pool size is a MEMORY decision rather than a core-count one: each worker isolate holds its own ~20 MB rank table and merge cache, so navigator.deviceMemory bounds it — eight lanes would be half a gigabyte resident before a row is read, which is how an iOS tab dies mid-file

Per-row billing capped at the limit and accumulated during the single pass, so changing the epochs is a multiplication while changing the limit needs another pass — keeping per-row counts for a two-million-row file would defeat the streaming design

Over-limit rows keep their own TEXT under a byte budget rather than an offset, because the offset is into the DECOMPRESSED stream and a .jsonl.gz cannot be seeked to one — rebuilding the export from offsets would silently produce garbage for most real inputs

First-party RFC 4180 CSV writer: control characters become visible escapes so one record is always one physical line, and the formula-injection guard EXEMPTS complete numeric literals — almost every column this tool writes is numeric, so the naive guard would corrupt nearly the whole file

A self-contained report.html built entirely with createElement and textContent — the file name and excerpted records come from a file epochcost did not write and the report is opened from file://, so string templating would let a training file put script into the report about itself

A permanent aria-live region OUTSIDE #app, and focus preserved across a full re-render via stable data-focus-key attributes with caret position, because render() calls app.replaceChildren() and typing an epoch count would otherwise lose the caret after every character

Both the footer and the event-log drawer MEMOISED, because both are built inside render(): the hosted feedback widget's link dies on the first re-render without the first, and the drawer silently stops opening without the second

Build-output gates in CI with the build BEFORE the tests so they cannot silently skip: no indexedDB/getDirectory-as-a-call/sessionStorage/document.cookie in dist/**, exactly one localStorage key checked as a STRING LITERAL because minification hoists the identifier, no console.* survivors, an absolute-URL allowlist by ORIGIN (a link is not a request), all three origins in both CSP directives, manifest-src named explicitly, and an apple-touch-icon whose pixels are decoded and alpha-checked — with the RANK TABLES excluded from the code scans, narrowly and provably, because a vocabulary genuinely contains 'sessionStorage' as a token

A negation-aware honesty gate over every user-facing string including the meta descriptions and JSON-LD, with a self-test proving it still catches a real claim and still permits a denial, plus a contrast gate that COMPUTES WCAG ratios for every text token against every background it can sit on

Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell with the sample and the DEFAULT vocabulary precached, the two legacy vocabularies deliberately left to HTTP caching, and NO runtimeCaching because workbox-expiration pulls IndexedDB into the bundle and would falsify the storage promise)

tools.name: crowdsize
tools.description: Drop a CSV of people and find out how many rows identify exactly one person, then generalise until they do not and leave with the rewritten file and a risk report. THIS RUN RESUMED AN ABANDONED 2026-08-14 BUILD — that run wrote the engine, the interface and 93 tests and died at the licensing step; nothing was deployed, the repo did not exist and there was no registry entry. The directory keeps its original date. QUEUE ORDER WAS NOT FOLLOWED and the reason is unchanged from 08-15: epochcost, leakspot and topicgap are the top three entries and all three remain blocked by standing-note rule 2 — epochcost's exact-token-count engine is chunkforge's (2026-08-10, six days) and its streaming-NDJSON-to-a-cost-figure architecture is runledger's (2026-08-09); leakspot and topicgap both rest on chunkforge's static-embedding engine. crowdsize is the first unblocked entry, which is the ghostdep and unfence precedent. The sensor debt was considered and deliberately not paid: IDEAS.md records that the 2026-08-11 hunt spent three adversarial rounds and killed all eight candidates, and asks for a hand-added idea rather than another speculative hunt. TWO ADVERSARIAL WORKFLOWS RAN (21 agents, 3.4M subagent tokens): five research lenses each attacked by an independent refuter, and five code-review dimensions each verified by a skeptic that reproduced or refuted every finding. 33 findings were CONFIRMED BY REPRODUCTION and the four HIGH ones changed the product. (1) THE TOOL WAS ASSERTING A PERSON BASIS IT HAD GUESSED. Until the user answers 'does each row describe a different person?', oneRowPerPerson is null — and the request sent the auto-guessed person key anyway, so the worker reported basis:'person-key', the interface withdrew its own 'these are rows, not people' warning, and READ-THIS-FIRST.txt stated 'counted in PEOPLE' as fact in a file destined for an ethics committee. One character: `=== false` rather than `!== true`. Verified in the browser — the headline now reads 'rows' until the question is answered. (2) THE HOMOGENEITY PASS ALLOCATED ONE JS ARRAY PER EQUIVALENCE CLASS, which on this tool's HEADLINE case — a mostly-unique file, one class per row — measured 302 MB of retained heap at a million rows and re-ran on every drag of a rung. That is the exact per-group allocation the counting engine was designed to avoid, reintroduced two files away. Replaced with a compressed row layout (prefix-sum offsets plus one Int32Array) and a bounded top-50: re-measured at 0.1 MB and 114 ms, a ~3,000x reduction, with a test proving the STRONGEST findings survive compaction rather than the first fifty seen. (3) EVERY INTERACTION DESTROYED KEYBOARD FOCUS. render() opens with app.replaceChildren() and every control calls it, so tabbing to a column checkbox and pressing Space left focus on with the operated element detached — a keyboard user re-tabbed from the top of the document after every single tick, which makes selecting a quasi-identifier set impossible. Controls now carry a stable data-focus-key that is read before teardown and restored after, caret position included. (4) THE RESULT WAS NEVER ANNOUNCED. There was no aria-live region anywhere: a sighted user watched 12,474 become 47 while a screen-reader user was told nothing. A permanent region now lives OUTSIDE #app, because one created inside it is destroyed by the same replaceChildren that necessitates it. (5) THE FEEDBACK LINK DIED ON FIRST INTERACTION — the memory note's exact trap, reproduced by planting a marker in the footer and watching it vanish after one click. footer() is now memoised, and the gate that was supposed to catch this was itself wrong: it counted CALL SITES and passed, because the single call sits inside render(). It now asserts the function returns the same node. (6) THE FORMULA-INJECTION GUARD CORRUPTED EVERY NEGATIVE NUMBER, prefixing an apostrophe onto -3.5 so a column of deltas or lab values arrived in Excel as text. Complete numeric literals are now exempt, which is safe because Excel evaluates -3.5 to -3.5 regardless, while -1+1 and @SUM(1+1) are still guarded. src/csv.ts had NO test file at all despite writing every artefact; it now has 18. browser_apis: File.stream() + TextDecoderStream — a several-hundred-megabyte CSV is never held as one string, and the decode is STREAMING so a multi-byte character split across a chunk boundary survives; the parser is verified by replaying documents at every possible split position

ONE module Web Worker, deliberately not a pool: from an arbitrary byte offset you cannot know whether the next quote opens or closes a field, and a newline inside a quoted field is ordinary data — which is exactly how a free-text notes column behaves. The parse is serial by necessity; the worker buys a main thread that never freezes

Dictionary-encoded columns plus open addressing over three Int32Arrays — 24 bytes per row, allocated once, no per-row objects. THE HASH IS NEVER THE KEY: a hash match is only a candidate and the row is confirmed by comparing integer codes, so class counts are exact and two groups can never silently merge into a k that is too HIGH, which is the one direction this tool must never be wrong in

A compressed per-class row layout (prefix-sum offsets + one Int32Array) for the homogeneity pass, replacing one JS array per equivalence class — measured 302 MB -> 0.1 MB at a million mostly-unique rows, which is the tool's headline case rather than its edge case

Generalisation applied to the DICTIONARY, not the rows: a column of 12,480 rows with 60 distinct values needs 60 transforms and a code remap, which is what makes the ladder feel like a control instead of a progress bar

Dates handled as string surgery and never through Date — `new Date('2019-03-04').getDate()` is 3 in New York and 4 in Auckland, so a Date-based year extractor gives two answers on two machines and is right on neither

A value that does not parse keeps its own distinct code, so every failure of the type inference can only make a class SMALLER and therefore only ever reports MORE risk — an invariant of the score that is explicitly NOT an invariant of the exported file, where such values are blanked

A first-party RFC 4180 writer: control characters become visible escapes so one record is always one physical line (the product is a count of rows, so a file whose row count depends on how you open it is unverifiable), formula injection guarded on = + - @ with complete numeric literals exempted so a column of negative numbers is not silently turned into text, ';' quoted for de/fr/es Excel, and a UTF-8 BOM asserted on the BYTES because Blob.text() strips it by spec

A self-contained risk-report.html built entirely with createElement and textContent — every value in it comes from a file crowdsize did not write and the report is opened from file://, so string templating would let a column header put script into the document about itself. It carries counts and distributions and never a person
A permanent aria-live region OUTSIDE #app, because render() calls app.replaceChildren() and a live region created inside it is destroyed by the very mechanism that makes one necessary

Focus preserved across a full re-render via stable data-focus-key attributes, caret position included — without it every tick of a checkbox dropped focus to <body> and detached the element just operated on

Build-output gates in CI with the build BEFORE the tests so they cannot silently skip: no indexedDB/getDirectory-as-a-call/sessionStorage/document.cookie in dist/**, exactly one localStorage key checked as a STRING LITERAL because minification hoists the identifier, no console.* survivors, an absolute-URL allowlist by ORIGIN (a link is not a request), both third-party origins in both CSP directives, manifest-src named explicitly rather than left to the default-src fallback, and an apple-touch-icon whose pixels are decoded and alpha-checked

A contrast gate that COMPUTES WCAG ratios for every text token against every background it can sit on, rather than trusting the eye that chose them

A source-hygiene gate over src/, tests/ and scripts/ that fails on any literal control byte — it caught a NUL keying the reference implementation the counter is verified against, and then caught one in a test written during this run

tools.name: unfence
tools.description: Paste a chat assistant's reply back into your project: it finds the file paths, diffs every block against your folder, and refuses to overwrite a real file with '// ... rest unchanged'. QUEUE ORDER WAS NOT FOLLOWED, for the reason the file provides: epochcost, leakspot and topicgap are the top three entries and all three are blocked by standing-note rule 2 — epochcost's tokenizer engine is chunkforge's (2026-08-10, five days), and its streaming-NDJSON-to-cost architecture is runledger's (2026-08-09); leakspot and topicgap both share chunkforge's static-embedding engine. unfence is the first unblocked entry, exactly the ghostdep precedent. The sensor debt was considered and deliberately not paid: IDEAS.md records that the 2026-08-11 hunt spent three adversarial rounds and killed all eight candidates, and asks for a hand-added idea rather than another speculative hunt. THE RESEARCH INVERTED THE PRODUCT BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN (13 agents, 1.33M tokens, every lens attacked by an independent refuter). (1) THE SPEC'S PRIMARY FEATURE IS THE MINORITY CASE. Measured over 10,988 fenced blocks in real multi-block programming answers, 3.82% carry a recoverable path and 96.18% do not — so unfence is not a path RECOVERY tool with an assignment fallback, it is a path ASSIGNMENT tool with recovery as an accelerator, and the queue with typeahead over the enumerated tree is the primary surface. (2) TWO OF THE SPEC'S FOUR CONVENTIONS ARE PHANTOMS: `title="..."` and `=== path ===` scored ZERO hits in 26,911 blocks, and the '35 separator hits' that justified the latter decompose to 37 BOLD-line hits, because the separator regex's delimiter class included `*`. Both are kept (five lines, cannot false-positive) but the two that actually fire were absent from the spec: Copilot Chat's mandated `// filepath:` comment and Aider's bare first line. (3) THE TRUNCATION RULE HAD TO BE DERIVED, TWICE. Brace balancing is undecidable here (registry.json finishes at depth +2 because of a brace inside a string; a Babel generator finishes at -1), and the replacement rule — regex the line at token.map[1]-1 — fails 4 of 23 controlled cases by two independent mechanisms and produced 44 FALSE truncations in 105 flags on a real corpus. What ships is arithmetic inside markdown-it's own coordinate system, closed = (map[1]-map[0]) >= contentLines + 2, verified 23/23 including list items, ordered lists, blockquotes, tilde fences and a bare unclosed fence at end of reply. A naive line scanner sees ZERO fences in the list-item case, which is the dominant shape of a multi-file answer. (4) ELISION CANNOT BE DETECTED FROM THE BLOCK. Simulating the modal case over 359 real files, the obvious 'new file is under half the size' rule catches ONE. The gate is the SHAPE OF THE DIFF — a hunk deleting >=12 lines while adding <=2 comment-only lines: 97.5% caught at a 2.56% false-alarm rate, phrasing- and language-independent. It must be overridable, because 0.68% of real revisions legitimately shrink below half. Bare `...` is refused as a marker outright: it is 92% of all marker-shaped lines AND the Python Ellipsis stub body. (5) THE GITIGNORE SUBSET LEAKS. Full matcher 99.95% agreement with real git check-ignore, documented subset 92.65% — and 1,060 of the subset's 1,405 disagreements INCLUDE a file git would have ignored, into a bundle the user pastes into a chat window. The full matcher is ninety lines and ships, tested differentially against real git. (6) FIVE BUGS THE BUILD CAUGHT ON ITSELF, THREE OF THEM IN THE BROWSER RATHER THAN THE UNIT TESTS. `createTwoFilesPatch` cannot express a deletion — measured, git apply returns rc=0 and leaves a ZERO-BYTE FILE, so the test asserts on file size rather than exit code. The space-in-path TAB is a post-process: passed as oldFileName it makes diff@9 C-quote the whole path (a tab is a byte below 0x20) and git answers 'No such file or directory'; appended after formatting it applies under both git apply and BSD patch. applyHunks got four trailing-newline cases wrong, caught by cross-checking every result against what real git produced. ESCAPE DID NOT CLOSE THE MODALS — the buttons filled the body and removed the hidden attribute directly, so the overlay was never on the stack the document-level Escape handler reads; the x control and the backdrop both worked, and three of sixteen exits failed silently. TWO BLOCKS ASSIGNED TO THE SAME PATH produced two `+++ b/...` CREATE stanzas, which git apply refuses outright — collapseDuplicates runs in the parser and never sees a user assignment. And a BARE FIRST-LINE PATH was being written into the file it named, so a created src/validate.js began with the text `src/validate.js`, a syntax error in every language. (7) `Newtonsoft.Json` PASSED THE PATHLIKE GATE, because .json is a known extension and the check was case-insensitive; a no-slash candidate now needs an all-lowercase extension, which also kills System.Text.Json and PIL.Image. (8) THE iOS NOTICE FIRED ON A DESKTOP MAC: the standard iPadOS heuristic (MacIntel + maxTouchPoints>1) false-positives under emulation and on any touch-capable Mac, so it is now gated behind the absence of showDirectoryPicker. (9) THE TOKEN TABLE WAS RE-FITTED FOR THIS BUILD over 2,170 hand-written files across 18 repositories and six languages (27.4 MB, 8,184,534 real o200k tokens, minified and vendored excluded). Bundle-level error over 500 simulated 200-file bundles: bytes/4 p50 -16.1% worst 29.3%; one global divisor p50 +0.3%; per-extension table p50 -1.4%, p5 -9.0%, p95 +5.2%, worst 12.6%. .json needs splitting by kind — lockfile 2.60 vs authored data 3.18. No tokenizer ships: exact o200k costs ~800 KB brotli by every route and this is the plumbing half. (10) VERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED: the patch the RUNNING BROWSER produced was extracted and applied by real git 2.50.1 — --check PASS, applied cleanly, src/validate.js created correctly, src/main.js left untouched so the 28 lines the elided block would have destroyed survive, and .github/workflows/ci.yml never created. All four overlays pass all four dismissal exits at 375px with real touch-type PointerEvents (16/16) at 44x44 hit areas; a full run issues requests for the page's own assets and NOTHING else. CI caught a cross-platform bug the local run could not: `git config --get core.ignorecase` exits 1 on a case-sensitive filesystem. 323 tests, four runtime dependencies.
browser_apis: File System Access opened in DEFAULT READ MODE — Chromium consults the write guard only for a readwrite picker, so under an IT policy blocking File System writes the whole read-only product still works: folder enumeration, a real diff against real bytes, elision refusal checked against actual on-disk content, and a git-apply-clean patch. Asking for readwrite up front turns that into a bare NotAllowedError at step one; write permission is requested later, from its own click

The feature detect is `'showDirectoryPicker' in window` and NOTHING else. FileSystemDirectoryHandle and createWritable both EXIST in Safari and Firefox for the Origin Private File System, so detecting on either promises folder writes on two browsers that cannot do them — and the failure arrives after the user has picked a folder and reviewed a diff

markdown-it for CommonMark tokenising, with truncation computed inside its own coordinate system and never by indexing back into raw document lines — a closing fence carrying container indentation never matches an anchored regex, and for a bare unclosed fence at end of reply the line at map[1]-1 IS the opening fence

diff@9 structuredPatch + formatPatch at context 3 (the package default is 4), with isDelete/isCreate set explicitly and the space-path tab appended AFTER formatting — never to an already-C-quoted path, since quotes are their own delimiter

client-zip: makeZip() returns a ReadableStream piped straight to a showSaveFilePicker handle, so a large backup is O(1) memory, and predictLength() is byte-exact — which is what makes the backup VERIFIABLE rather than merely written. It is re-opened and checked against that length and the PK\x05\x06 end-of-archive signature before one byte of the folder changes

createWritable() with NO keepExistingData, ever: measured, a 27-byte file rewritten with 5 bytes under that flag stays 27 bytes and reads XXXXXNAL-CONTENT-1234567890 — and the modal case here is a reply that SHORTENS a file, so it would splice the old tail on constantly and plausibly enough that per-hunk review would not catch it. close() is never called on a stream that was not fully written

Segment-by-segment path resolution, because getFileHandle() cannot take a path (measured: TypeError, not SecurityError) — and an intermediate directory that does not already exist requires explicit confirmation, or a hallucinated srcc/app.ts silently materialises a new tree that looks like an ordinary new file in the review

A first-party gitignore matcher: nested files carried as a rule stack evaluated deepest-last, top-down pruning that reproduces 'a negation cannot re-include under an excluded directory' for free, full ** / character-class / POSIX-class / escape support, case-insensitive by default to match git on APFS and Windows — and a report of negations that can never fire, which no other tool does

A hardcoded secret refusal list that is INDEPENDENT of .gitignore and has no negation mechanism, closing the two-step attack where a reply rewrites .gitignore to un-hide .env and the user pastes the next bundle into a chat window themselves. Build output is excluded unconditionally because a bundler bakes .env values in as string literals

Web Worker (module) holding every diff and every parse — the cost of a diff is its EDIT DISTANCE, so 5,000 lines at 1% changed is 4 ms and the same file fully rewritten is two seconds, and one badly-behaved block would freeze the interface mid-review
EOL normalised to LF before diffing and restored on write: a CRLF file against an LF reply of identical text otherwise produces one hunk of ten thousand lines carrying no information

A plan/write hash check — every target is re-read immediately before writing and skipped if it changed while the user was reading the diff, which is the only defence against clobbering an editor autosave

One programmatic download per user gesture, every artefact in a single zip, triggered synchronously inside the click handler — Chromium flips a tab to PROMPT_BEFORE_DOWNLOAD after the first, and a missed bubble means artefacts two to four silently never arrive

Reply content rendered exclusively through textContent and createElement, asserted by a build gate: a prose paragraph in an untrusted reply would otherwise be able to fire an exfiltration beacon on paste. CSP names manifest-src 'self' explicitly, or the tool cannot install as a PWA

Build-output gates in CI with the build BEFORE the tests so they cannot silently skip: no IndexedDB/OPFS/sessionStorage/cookies in dist/** (getDirectory matched as a CALL, because a substring test also matches getDirectoryHandle — the ordinary API this whole tool is built on), no console.* survivors, an absolute-URL allowlist, both origins in both CSP directives, and an apple-touch-icon whose pixels are decoded and alpha-checked

A negation-aware honesty gate over user-facing text that fails the build on any promise of safety, and a source gate that scans CODE rather than comments — its first version fired on the comment in fs/write.ts explaining why keepExistingData must never be used

Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell with both samples precached and NO runtimeCaching, because workbox-expiration pulls IndexedDB into the bundle and would falsify the storage promise). On desktop Chromium an installed PWA also earns extended File System Access permission

tools.name: docxray
tools.description: See what is still hiding inside a Word file before you email it: every tracked change with its author, every comment including the resolved ones, hidden text, and the part of each photograph that was cropped away but not removed. THIS RUN RESUMED AN ABANDONED 2026-08-12 BUILD — that run scaffolded the project, wrote src/xml.ts and died; nothing was deployed, the repo did not exist and there was no registry entry. The directory keeps its original date. Four investigations and four adversarial refutations (990k subagent tokens) ran against the spec; the refutations changed the product, not just the code. (1) THE PITCH WAS FALSE AND WAS REWRITTEN. IDEAS.md claimed Mac/web/iPad users have 'no way to see' this and that Document Inspector is the only route. Refuted: Word for Mac has Review > All Markup and a Reviewing Pane with counts, a Preferences setting that WARNS before sending a file with tracked changes, and Compress Pictures > 'Delete cropped areas of pictures'; Word's own Crop tool greys out and shows the recoverable region; LibreOffice shows crop values numerically and is free on every platform. What survives measurement, and what the interface now says, is narrower and true: Word's ONE-PASS Document Inspector is Windows-only (Microsoft's own words: Word for Mac 'doesn't have a document inspector', and inspection 'isn't currently possible in Word for the web'), it removes without showing, and no free client-side tool audits every image in a document at once and reports crop geometry. The query 'check word document for tracked changes before sending' returns zero third-party tools. (2) THE REFUTER FOUND A REAL BUG IN SHIPPED CODE. comments.ts tested w15:done against '0' and 'false' only — ST_OnOff has THREE false spellings, so done='off' reported a LIVE comment thread as resolved, which is the wrong direction for this tool to be wrong in. Fixed, with a regression test that fails when reintroduced. (3) THE mc:AlternateContent DOUBLE-COUNT IS THE CENTRAL TRAVERSAL BUG AND IT REACHES THE HEADLINE FEATURE. Word writes a text box's content TWICE — a DrawingML shape in mc:Choice and a VML shape in mc:Fallback — and measured in a real corpus, one AlternateContent yields two w:txbxContent (1->2, 2->4, 7->14). The refuter added the case the report missed: in one file the two branches hold a w:drawing and a w:pict of the SAME PICTURE, so a naive walker reports 2 cropped photographs where there is 1, with two different ratios because the two encodings round differently. walkContent takes exactly one branch. PROVEN ON THE SHIPPED SAMPLE: the parts contain 31 revision ELEMENTS and the tool reports 30 — the difference is the Fallback copy. (4) THE CROP UNITS ARE TWO DIFFERENT SYSTEMS FOR ONE IDEA. a:srcRect is ST_Percentage in thousandths of a percent (and legally also a '25%' string, both branches parsed); v:imagedata cropleft is a plain FRACTION. Reading one with the other's scale is off by four orders of magnitude and shows as no crop at all. Both ship, both are tested, and the values are INSETS not coordinates — read as coordinates, l=0.25/r=0.25 gives a visible width of zero where the truth is half the image. (5) MOST a:srcRect ELEMENTS ARE NOT CROPS: measured 12 in a 12-document corpus, 9 of them empty. Reporting on the element's presence would flag a crop on nearly every document containing a picture. (6) w:vanish IS A TOGGLE THAT CAN BE TURNED OFF, and this is not hypothetical — LibreOffice's exporter emits <w:vanish w:val='false'/> at docxattributeoutput.cxx:8731, so any file that has been through it would report a document full of hidden text that has none. It is also usually set on a STYLE rather than a run, so the style cascade is resolved (docDefaults -> paragraph style chain -> character style chain -> direct), and the finding NAMES the style that hides the text. (7) WHITE-ON-WHITE IS REPORTED AS A WCAG CONTRAST RATIO, NOT A COLOUR MATCH. The background is w:shd/@w:fill and never @w:color (which is the shading PATTERN foreground), w:highlight is a 17-name enumeration that wins over shading, and theme colours resolve through TWO hops — clrSchemeMapping then theme1.xml, where a sysClr slot's colour is @lastClr and @val is a system-colour NAME. Getting the first hop wrong reports white text on a BLACK cell as invisible, which is a false positive on perfectly legible text and would destroy trust in every other finding. 'auto' is never parsed as a colour. (8) THE rsid CLAIM WAS VERIFIED AND MADE STRONGER. Microsoft's own implementer note: Word 'generates a random number for every rsid that is not necessarily larger than all earlier ones in the same file'; independently, the table was measured numerically SORTED in 12 of 12 real files, so the observable order is a sort and not a history. Two independent reasons. No chronology, ever, enforced by a structural CI gate. The count is reported as an UPPER BOUND because 33-79% of table entries in that corpus referenced text no longer in the document. (9) MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE ARCHITECTURE: unzipSync over a 60 MiB package costs ~67 MiB of extra heap, the same call FILTERED to XML/rels costs a few hundred KB, and streaming measured SLOWER (39ms vs 32ms) because the whole file is already an ArrayBuffer before fflate sees it. Media is extracted one entry at a time and only for pictures that carry a crop. (10) A PASSWORD-PROTECTED .docx IS NOT A ZIP but an OLE2/CFB container; it is detected by magic bytes FIRST and named, because telling somebody their contract is corrupt when it is merely encrypted is a bad answer. (11) BUGS THE BUILD CAUGHT ON ITSELF: a CSV control-character regex was written by pasting literal control bytes (caught by the source-hygiene gate, now a code-point predicate); the honesty gate's first version scanned raw source and fired on a COMMENT explaining the tool makes no such claim, because a template-literal regex matched from the end of one backtick string to the start of the next, swallowing the code between; the network gate failed on a footer LINK to benrichardson.dev (a link is not a request); and the apple-touch-icon gate rejected a perfectly opaque RGBA icon on colour type alone, so it now decodes the pixels and checks the alpha channel. (12) VERIFIED IN THE BROWSER, NOT ASSERTED: the crop reveal was checked BY PIXEL — inside the outline luminance 212, outside 56, and 194 amber pixels tracing the dashed rectangle; all five overlays pass all four dismissal exits at 375px with real touch-type PointerEvents (20/20) with 44x44 hit areas; the full run issues requests for the page's own assets and the sample and NOTHING else; and the exported report is 107 KB with no script, link or src, four embedded reveals, and the document's own markup escaped. A lazy-loading bug was found and fixed in the browser: the reveals carried loading='lazy', which saves no network on a data URL and left the headline finding rendering as four empty boxes in a background tab. 116 tests, one runtime dependency.

The first mc:Choice is taken unconditionally, which is a STATED simplification rather than the full algorithm: @Requires holds prefixes and this parser discards prefix bindings at parse time, so they cannot be resolved. It is safe here because both branches carry the same w:txbxContent and the requirement is 'exactly one', not 'which one'

In real documents media is STORED rather than deflated, so the saving is a copy and an allocation, not a decompression

WMF/EMF/TIFF media is named as undecodable rather than thrown on

Style-cascade resolution for w:vanish (docDefaults -> paragraph style chain -> character style chain -> direct rPr), tri-state at every layer so a later layer can turn a property OFF, with basedOn cycles bounded — and w:pPr/w:rPr deliberately excluded, because that is the PARAGRAPH MARK's formatting and using it would report every run in a hidden block as separately hidden

WCAG contrast against the real background: w:shd/@w:fill (never @w:color, the pattern foreground), w:highlight's 17-name enumeration winning over shading, and theme colours resolved through clrSchemeMapping then theme1.xml with a sysClr slot read from @lastClr

Comment threading joined on the LAST paragraph's w14:paraId — taking the first works on every single-paragraph comment then silently breaks on the long substantive one — with collisions DETECTED and the threading withdrawn rather than shown wrong, because paraId is four bytes and has been measured colliding within one real document

Field-instruction reassembly across runs between fldChar begin and separate, including w:delInstrText where a deleted HYPERLINK to a local path hides; and relationship-target analysis that flags an ORPHAN link whose visible text was deleted while the URL was left behind

Part discovery through the RELATIONSHIP GRAPH rather than by filename, which is what reaches the glossary document — a complete second WordprocessingML document holding building blocks and AutoText that almost nothing scans

First-party RFC 4180 CSV writer with control characters as visible escapes so one record is always one physical line, a formula-injection guard leading WITH forced quoting, ';' quoting for de/fr/es Excel, UTF-8 BOM and CRLF

A self-contained disclosure-report.html built entirely with createElement and textContent — every value in it is third-party content from an untrusted file and the report is opened from file://, so string templating would let a document put script into the report about itself. No script, no link, no src, verified in the browser

tools.name: ghostdep
tools.description: Check that the packages an AI told you to install actually exist, then leave with a pinned, hash-locked lockfile. THE RUN FIRST SPENT THREE ADVERSARIAL ROUNDS HUNTING A LIVE-SENSOR TOOL AND FOUND NONE THAT SURVIVED — eight candidates generated, all eight refuted, findings and the bar recorded in IDEAS.md. Six of the eight died on one of exactly two things: a free client-side browser incumbent (sonavyx does clap-to-RT60 with a 24-bit IR export; phyphox ships the bouncing-ball experiment verbatim; eight free stop-motion tools rank for that query) or a number needing a calibration reference the page cannot enforce. ghostdep was then built as the first queue entry not blocked by standing-note rule 2 (epochcost shares the tokenizer engine with runledger 2026-08-09; leakspot and topicgap share the embedding engine with chunkforge 2026-08-10). (1) THE LOAD-BEARING RULE IS THAT A FAILED LOOKUP IS NEVER A MISSING PACKAGE. 'error' and 'missing' are separate states through the interface and every artefact, because a dropped request reported as a hallucinated package is the most damaging thing this tool could say. (2) THE DISTANCE FUNCTION IS TRUE DAMERAU-LEVENSHTEIN, NOT OSA, and that is a correctness requirement rather than a preference: almost every npm package with that name implements OSA, which answers 3 for d('ca','abc') where the truth is 2, and OSA violates the triangle inequality — a BK-tree is only correct over a metric, and the failure mode is a neighbour that silently never comes back, on a tool whose whole job is finding it. A PRUNING BUG OF EXACTLY THAT SHAPE WAS WRITTEN AND CAUGHT: passing the distance cutoff into the tree's own node comparison under-estimates d and shifts the child-bucket window down, dropping subtrees that do contain matches. Verified by reintroducing it — 5 of 8 tree tests fail, including the headline python-dateutils -> python-dateutil case. A brute-force agreement test over 1,500 real names at three budgets ships. (3) THE THRESHOLDS ARE THE PRODUCT. ms, qs and ws are three real npm packages one edit apart, each downloaded tens of millions of times weekly, so any flat 'within one edit of something popular' rule fires on all three in the first ten seconds. The edit budget scales with name length (two-character names get a budget of zero) and a neighbour is mentioned only when far more popular; both are sliders with the live match list underneath. (4) THE DRY-RUN AGAINST THE LIVE REGISTRIES FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS THE UNIT TESTS DID NOT. The sample reported 10 non-existent packages where 7 were planted, because candidate dedup lowercased but did not apply PEP 503 — langchain_communty and langchain-communty are the SAME PyPI project and were counted twice. And pillow was flagged as 'close to a bigger name' against willow, PyYAML against pyaml, because the popularity-ratio test was skipped for every PyPI package: pypistats.org sends no access-control-allow-origin header at all, so a browser cannot read PyPI download counts, and the code forgot the bundled table already knows pillow is rank 68. Own-popularity now comes from the table when the registry cannot supply it. Both fixed and re-verified: 22 checked, exactly 7 missing, zero false flags. (5) ENDPOINTS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY HABIT. npm's obvious GET /{name} is 6,878,486 bytes for react and 2.9 MB even with the abbreviated Accept header; GET /{name}/latest is ~2 KB and 404s cleanly. PyPI's PEP 691 simple index is served as api-version 1.4, i.e. PEP 700, so ONE request returns existence, versions, per-file upload-time, size, yanked and sha256 — which is what makes the --require-hashes artefact real. The full npm packument is fetched ONLY for packages below 50k weekly downloads, which is exactly where age is the question and exactly where the document is small. (6) THE REQUIREMENTS FILE CARRIES ITS OWN LIMITATION INSIDE IT: pip --require-hashes demands every transitive dependency be pinned and hashed, and ghostdep only sees the names you pasted, so the file says so and names pip-compile --generate-hashes rather than failing on first use with an error that does not explain itself. (7) OTHER BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT: the URL guard /^https?/ matched httpx — one of the most-installed packages on PyPI — and silently dropped it as a URL; the wheel-filename matcher built its character class and THEN escaped regex metacharacters, escaping the brackets it had just inserted, so it matched nothing for every punctuated name (ruamel.yaml, zope.interface); the import map was being applied to pip install lines, rewriting a user's 'flask' to 'Flask' for no purpose since PEP 503 makes them one project; a const named self in the worker's message handler would have put the earlier self.postMessage into a temporal dead zone; and the CSV writer's control-character class was written with LITERAL control bytes, caught by the source-hygiene gate. (8) THE HONESTY GATE FIRED ON ITS OWN DISCLAIMER on first run and is now negation-aware, with a self-test proving it still catches a real claim. There is no 'malicious' verdict and no 'safe' verdict, by construction. NOT DEPLOYED TO ITS CUSTOM DOMAIN: the benrichardson.dev Cloudflare zone is at its hard 200-record cap (error 81045) and a full audit found no reclaimable slot — 185 of 186 Pages CNAMEs are claimed by a live repo and the one that is not is www, a live 301. tools.name: chunkforge
tools.description: Drop your own documents, mark the passage each failing query should have returned, and watch what comes back as you drag the chunk-size slider — then take the splitter config. Adversarial research (43 agents, six lenses, every finding attacked by an independent skeptic) inverted six load-bearing pieces of the spec and reshaped the metric. (1) THE SPEC'S EMBEDDING PATH CANNOT RUN. @huggingface/transformers needs config.json, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json and special_tokens_map.json at the model repo root; all four 404, and even given them the graph's only output is sentence_embedding while the feature-extraction pipeline reads last_hidden_state ?? logits ?? token_embeddings. The runtime-free table reader is the only path, not an optimisation: static-retrieval-mrl-en-v1's whole graph is Gather -> DequantizeLinear -> ReduceMean, so an embedding is the mean of some uint8 rows, read out with a ~200-line protobuf reader. Measured 3,000 chunks of ~800 characters embedded in 220 ms, which is what makes a live slider possible at all. (2) IDF-WEIGHTED POOLING IS A MEASURED REGRESSION AND WAS CUT. It was in the design on one anecdote inherited from searchpack. On BEIR SciFact (300 queries, harness validated by reproducing this model's own published MTEB figures to four decimals) plain mean scores nDCG@10 0.5938 against 0.5648 weighted, paired bootstrap over 10,000 resamples giving P(weighted better) = 0.007; the anecdote was a score-SCALE artefact, gold-to-random separation moving only 0.3595 -> 0.3667. Worse here specifically: weights drawn from the chunking move with the slider — eight points of instrument drift, the same magnitude as the effect being measured. The weights survive only as a no-signal threshold, which is not a score. (3) K MUST BE DERIVED FROM A CONTEXT BUDGET, NOT FIXED — the correction that makes the whole comparison valid. At a fixed top-10 a 128-token chunking returns ~1,270 tokens and an 8,192-token chunking returns ~54,080, so 'recall rises with chunk size' is arithmetic. k = floor(budget / size), and every setting is judged at the same price. A ZERO-SKILL CHANCE LEVEL is drawn beside every score in closed form (1 - C(n-h,k)/C(n,k)): on the shipped sample 96-token chunks score a perfect 3 of 3 at a 43% chance level, which without that column reads identically to the genuinely good row. A HIT IS BINARY CHARACTER OVERLAP, not a fraction of the marked span — measured against sloppy marking a fractional score moves -0.26 while binary overlap moves +0.02. NO WINNER IS DECLARED (separating two close settings needs ~6 one-way discordant queries; nobody types six), no percentage is printed without its denominator, and the published chunking-evaluation metric names (recall, precision, IoU) are deliberately never used over a chunkforge number. (4) THE MODERN PDF.JS BUILD IS A WHITE PAGE ON EVERY IPHONE BELOW iOS 18.4. build/pdf.mjs contains `if (typeof Iterator.prototype.join !== "function")` unguarded at module top level — typeof protects a bare identifier, NOT a property access on one — plus bare Promise.withResolvers, Promise.try, Uint8Array.toHex and Math.sumPrecise. The legacy build ships, at about 16 kB gzipped. Also: without cMapUrl a CJK PDF resolves, paginates and returns items: [] with only a console warning, so the 169 predefined CMaps are served from this origin, fetched only when a document needs one and deliberately not precached; and transform[3] is exactly 0 for text rotated 90 degrees, so the type size is hypot(transform[2], transform[3]). (5) SORTING LINES BY Y IS WHAT BREAKS TWO-COLUMN PDFs. Real two-column producers emit each column contiguously, so content-stream order IS reading order and a y-sort interleaves them; column detectors built to repair the damage were measured finding ZERO columns on a genuine two-column paper and up to sixteen spurious ones on pages containing tables, where the gutter was a cell boundary. No column detector ships. Lines keep document order with a geometric fallback gated on an absolute allowance rather than a proportion — a five-line title page with one upward jump scored 0.75 on a ratio and was wrongly scrambled. (6) THE SPLITTER IS VERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED. The recursive strategy is compared against langchain-text-splitters 0.3.11 ITSELF, via a fixture generated by running the library, and matches chunk for chunk and string for string across all seven size and overlap settings including the degenerate 80-token case where the reference emits oversized chunks; the default separator ladder was read out of the source (no sentence rung, so it will cut a sentence in half) rather than remembered, and adding one would make chunkforge's chunks nicer than the config it hands you. Byte-level BPE was written first-party rather than pulling gpt-tokenizer's 53 MB barrel — identical ids to the reference for cl100k_base and o200k_base across ten edge cases and an 11,003-token document, first token to last, with offsets that round-trip through emoji and umlauts; the Rust (?i:) inline group is a JavaScript syntax error and is translated only when it is a plain literal alternation, refused otherwise. Bugs the tests and the dry-run caught: chanceOfHit returned 1 instead of 0 for k=0 when every chunk touched the span (found by brute-force enumeration of every k-subset); the sweep carried overlap as an ABSOLUTE count, so 200 tokens at size 96 clamped to 95 and made the stride ONE TOKEN — 11,014 chunks from an 11,000-token document, crowding out every real row; two literal NUL bytes were written into src/, one keying the BPE merge table where both sides agreed so every test passed; the running-header stripper used index-based bands that assume visual order and leaked a page number; and a 1.55x paragraph threshold merged four paragraphs into one 1,537-character block. THE SAMPLE'S OWN PLAN WAS WRONG TWICE and the test that caught it is shipped: it was written so one query would favour small chunks, measured it favoured large ones, and after the metric changed the real finding became cost — recursive 1024/200, the most-copied config anywhere, returns all three marked answers for 3,724 retrieved tokens per query at a 29% chance level while heading-aware at the same size returns the same three for 1,408 at 10%. 284 tests; all five overlays pass all four dismissal exits at 375px with real touch-type PointerEvents.
browser_apis: A runtime-free ONNX reader (~200 lines of protobuf walking) that lifts one quantised uint8 tensor out of static-retrieval-mrl-en-v1 by NAME rather than by offset — 26 KB of JavaScript instead of 11 MB of WASM, which is the only reason a whole corpus can be re-embedded between two frames of a slider drag. GitHub Pages cannot send COOP/COEP, so onnxruntime-web would be pinned to a single WASM thread anyway

First-party byte-level BPE read straight from tokenizer.json — verified token-for-token against gpt-tokenizer for cl100k_base and o200k_base over an 11,003-token document. Three things a plausible implementation gets wrong: the pre-tokenizer regex is Rust's, and its (?i:'s|'t|...) inline group is a JavaScript syntax error; merges ship as space-joined STRINGS in cl100k and as two-element ARRAYS in ModernBERT and Qwen, and a reader handling one silently produces a vocabulary with no merges that still 'works' at one token per byte; and BPE operates on bytes while the splitters slice UTF-16 characters, so every piece is mapped back through a byte-to-character index

First-party WordPiece with OFFSETS — the normaliser carries a character map rather than returning a string, because accent stripping, lowercasing and control-character removal none of them preserve length, and every chunk boundary downstream is a character offset

TWO TOKENIZERS, kept strictly apart: the BOUNDARY tokenizer is the user's own embedding model's, and is what '512 tokens' means; the SCORING tokenizer is the static model's WordPiece and exists only to index a lookup table. Its counts are never shown. Conflating them would hand back a number that is wrong in the user's pipeline and flagged by nothing downstream

Line ordering by CONTENT-STREAM order with a geometric fallback, and no column detector at all — the opposite of the obvious design, because real two-column producers already emit reading order and a y-sort is what interleaves them

Running-header removal by two rules, either sufficient: a document-wide count for the header identical on every page, and a CONSECUTIVE-RUN rule for the one that changes per section, which never reaches a document-wide proportion. Bands are geometric, not index-based, because the line list is in producer order and a footer drawn before the body lands at index 1

Web Worker (module) that RETAINS the parsed corpus and the token indices — a slider move is array slicing plus a binary search, never re-tokenization, which is the difference between a control and a progress bar

Cache API for the two model files, pinned to an immutable revision and fetched with credentials omitted, so every run after the first is fully offline and the tool can honestly claim 'your documents never leave the tab' rather than the false 'no network'

First-party RFC 4180 CSV writer — control characters become visible escapes so one record is always one physical line, formula-injection guard on =+-@ leads WITH forced quoting, ';' quoting for de/fr/es Excel, UTF-8 BOM and CRLF
A self-contained report.html built with no script, no link and no src, with every document name and query string escaped — they are user input and the file is opened from file://
ONE zip from ONE click (fflate), because Safari silently suppresses every programmatic download after the first in a single gesture and Chrome's limiter turns the second into a permission prompt

Build-output gates run in CI with the build BEFORE the tests so they cannot silently skip: no indexedDB / getDirectory / sessionStorage / document.cookie anywhere in dist/**, exactly one localStorage key checked as a STRING LITERAL because minification hoists it into a single-letter variable, no console.* survivors, and both third-party origins named in both CSP directives
A source-hygiene gate that fails on any literal control byte in src/ — it caught two real ones, including a NUL keying the BPE merge table where both sides of the lookup agreed so every test passed

Four-way overlay dismissal on all five overlays, verified at 375px with real touch-type PointerEvents rather than .click(), including the [hidden] baseline and elementFromPoint at the viewport centre after every close
